canonical_topic: How natural gas pipelines physically move gas
definition: Pipelines move gas by maintaining a pressure differential — high pressure at the inlet and low pressure at the outlet — with intermediate compressor stations on long pipelines acting like fans to keep gas flowing.
core_idea: Gas flow through a pipeline is driven purely by engineered pressure gradients, reinforced periodically by compressor stations over long distances.
key_points: Flow is created by high pressure at one end and low pressure at the other end of the pipe.
Long pipelines use intermediate compressor stations to re-establish the pressure gradient along the route.
relationships: Sets up the operational-continuity requirement that motivates natural gas storage.
